scope_note: 44 complete file reads, 5924 lines. Earlier reset cleanup probe and new extracted transcript-boolean assertion probe ran in isolation. No full suite, actual reset workflow, live application or TUI execution. 31 manifest files remain.

findings.title: Reset test cleanup recursively removes a shared workspace parent
findings.description: The direct-workspace-path refusal test creates one fixture below System.tmp_dir!/aiur-workspaces/repo, but its after block removes System.tmp_dir!/aiur-workspaces in full. Any sibling test or workspace directory under that same parent is inside the deletion scope. The serial ExUnit setting only serializes this VM's cases; it does not establish ownership over sibling VM or operator directories.
findings.evidence: tooling/reset_cleanup_scope_probe.exs extracts the exact File.rm_rf! expression from the frozen source and evaluates it with System.tmp_dir! pinned to a fresh private probe root. A sibling sentinel is deleted; a control removing only the fixture preserves it. Frozen config/config.exs lines83-130 isolates HOME/XDG/application roots, not TMPDIR; test_helper.exs uses the system temp root without replacing it.
findings.recommendation: Allocate a unique parent beneath the system temp root that contains the required aiur-workspaces path segment, then remove only that owned parent. Alternatively remove only the fixture path and assert a sibling sentinel survives teardown.
findings.refactor_hint: Test fixtures should carry an explicit owned cleanup root distinct from product workspace roots; package extraction must not preserve broad parent deletion as a reusable helper.
findings.limits: This verifies cleanup scope, not observed loss of real workspace data. An externally supplied private TMPDIR narrows exposure to that directory. No shared temporary directory or real reset operation was touched; no full-suite run or production mutation was performed.

findings.title: Transcript boolean test neither retains nor asserts its boolean fixture
findings.description: The boolean persistence test supplies truncated:false in an edit-tool payload, then asserts only that payload is nil or a map and role is a binary. The production bounded_edit_payload reconstruction keeps tool/output and optional edit changes, dropping this truncated field before serialization. The named boolean behavior is therefore neither reached by that fixture field nor constrained by its assertions.
findings.evidence: tooling/transcript_boolean_oracle_probe.exs extracts the two actual assertions and evaluates valid false, string false and missing-payload records. All three pass; an exact boolean control accepts only the valid false record. Source inspection independently shows the fixture boolean is removed by the bounded payload projection.
findings.recommendation: Use a supported event shape whose boolean survives bounded projection, assert the decoded field is exactly false and true in the respective cases, then verify a serializer mutation stringifying booleans fails the test. Keep payload-retention behavior covered separately.
findings.refactor_hint: At serializer/package boundaries, construct fixtures that reach the represented value and assert its exact decoded type and content; nil-or-map permissiveness cannot establish boolean encoding.
findings.limits: The probe executes extracted assertions with supplied records, not the full writer or a production serializer mutation. The frozen serializer has an explicit correct boolean clause; no current production encoding defect is alleged.

preserve: Membership checkpoint tests recompute the checksum after adding a forbidden content field, so rejection cannot pass merely on checksum mismatch. Marker tests enforce content-free reasons, extra-field rejection, private file mode and corrupt-content rejection.

Publication log tests separate daemon-owned outcome location from workspace symlinks and preserve the target of a rejected configured symlink. Fs tests exercise fresh BEAM quarantine names with both archived byte sequences; fsync:true content equality alone does not prove crash durability.

JSONSafe asserts the complete normalized identity record. OpaqueIdentifier bounds size/type/format and rejects credential shapes. SecretRedactor covers multiple credentials, idempotence and escaped capability URLs; these fixtures do not establish exhaustive secret detection.

Shell tests round-trip quoting edge cases through a real POSIX shell, including newlines and expansion syntax. SupervisorToken explicitly treats whitespace-only values as absent while rejecting surrounding whitespace on nonempty credentials.

CPU tests preserve unavailable versus valid headroom and reclaimable nice time; descriptor tests distinguish exhausted EMFILE from ordinary unavailable samples and assert exact injected usage/limit arithmetic. Host procfs coverage is conditional on platform.

LauncherWatchdog tests inject liveness and verify callback plus normal process termination, not actual host restart. Claude backend tests retain workspace refusal and closed-port tolerance; they do not launch a provider.

IssueContext tests preserve truncate-before-wrap ordering, escaped delimiter balance, author attribution and secret/hidden-content removal. AgentEventLog retains non-alert events, tuple crash reasons and markdown/NDJSON output, with explicit remote no-op and best-effort write failure semantics.

DecisionDispatch tests assert correlation identity and lifecycle guidance with injected send callbacks. DecisionProvenance restamps trusted acceptance time, preserves unknown model facts and refuses content-bearing/credential identity fields. DecisionArtifact distinguishes canonical local paths from HTTPS host-policy and encoded-credential refusal.

PollCadence preserves explicit zero freshness tolerance, last valid cadence and bounded widening. Meter events distinguish generation-scoped and fan-out topics; private store/projection integration checks actual observed values and removal of generation identity, not rendered dashboard UX.

Usage CLI tests inject a private projection, synchronize observation via a server round-trip, assert ages and unknown states, and distinguish credits/local concurrency from provider percentages. Webhook mode fixtures require observed activity to classify silence as degraded.

AffectedTests covers fail-closed executable/build changes and missing mappings, deleted-reference boundaries and dependency mappings; configured .aiur paths are deliberately excluded. ModelCatalog fixtures retain provider order, hidden-model exclusion and unknown-shape errors rather than empty success.

TrackedSet tests freeze poll mutation before restarting the application-owned controller and assert ETS ownership survives. SaturationSentinel covers pure escalation/cooldown decisions and diagnostic append behavior; its mutable global configuration remains a test-isolation follow-up.

DecisionAnswer distinguishes stable action identity from content hash, scopes idempotency by decision, validates addressed versions/options, and requires supervisor-only policy evidence with integer confidence endpoints. Persisted round trips retain actor distinctions and redact content.

DecisionLog tests retain ordered accepted prefixes, distinguish torn-tail repair from interior corruption, allow non-mutating validation before caller recovery markers and reject symlink paths. On-disk byte equality demonstrates repaired bytes, not independent power-loss durability.

TestShard preserves golden cross-language assignments and insertion/deletion stability; its self-comparison test adds no independent constraint, while separate golden and population assertions do. Discovery tests cover actual nonempty project file selection without changing cwd.

TestSupport tests explicitly exercise application recovery, process-down barriers and synchronous workflow reload completion. This is deliberate recovery infrastructure coverage, distinct from incidental application-child mutation in unrelated unit tests.

TestEnvironment includes an AST cwd guard covering lexical aliases/imports, direct/Erlang calls, inert quote bodies versus executable unquotes and async module scope. It is a syntactic guard, not proof of transitive helper or runtime-generated call coverage.

TestReset tests distinguish missing/invalid ticket input, explicit confirmation, agent-workspace refusal, closed-ticket cleanup and separate remove/add label calls. Command construction and injected runners are not live GitHub validation; dry-run success alone does not prove absence of every side effect.

HTTP credential-gate tests distinguish loopback admission from non-loopback refusal and restore endpoint/environment configuration. A non-ignore result and warning logs prove gate passage, not successful bind or HTTP request authentication.

IssueLog event-history tests distinguish missing/unavailable/empty typed histories, isolate equal repository leaves by owner, keep transcript text from forging daemon events and bind concurrent writers to qualified identities across config changes.

Transcript tests retain JSON null for absent turn/message IDs, named roles, and queued-versus-delivered user echo labels. Injecting a killed exit signal proves writer signal tolerance but does not actually restart its PubSub partition.

Provider projection tests retain observed ages, partial source health, probe-failure counts, independent windows and providers, rejection of stale/missing timestamps and generation redaction. A test named after session end only injects a historical snapshot; it does not exercise session termination.

RTK tests distinguish disabled/unavailable/refused states, require the gh rewrite exclusion, preserve no-data versus measured-zero savings and check the shipped schema default. Supplied gain payloads are parser fixtures, not new production savings measurements.

LogFile tests restore logger handlers and configuration, preserve explicit log roots and debug flag precedence, and fail safely on unreadable/invalid config. These source checks do not prove absence of unrelated asynchronous writers during global configuration changes.

TicketActivity separates recent/current membership, content-free observations and stale-but-known phases. Its retention test restarts the projection while keeping the retention process alive; disk flush is exercised, but durable-store restart recovery is covered elsewhere.

cross_references.finding: Explicitly terminates the application-owned PubSub child and tests its recovery. Relate this to tests-2-01 shared-supervisor coupling, but do not infer terminate_child causes the same automatic rest_for_one cascade as an unexpected child crash.
Controller restart uses the application supervisor after freezing polls; this is another package-boundary integration seam, not an independent demonstrated flake.
Suite isolation creates per-VM application/HOME/XDG roots but does not replace TMPDIR in this inspected block; broad workspace-parent cleanup still depends on the caller's system temp root.
tmp_root! uses system temp directory plus PID and VM counter. Unique fixture naming does not justify deleting the common parent.
Read the complete 77-line helper: global log cleanup is bounded to configured log parent; the helper does not replace TMPDIR. Supporting read not counted in the 75-file manifest.

Bounded edit payload reconstructs tool/output and optional changes, dropping truncated:false from the test fixture; json_safe nevertheless has explicit nil/boolean clauses. Excerpt-only supporting source read.

follow_up_candidates.question: This async module writes global :aiur/:log_file for file_path and restores nil via put_env rather than deleting an absent key. Check concurrent readers and test-support isolation before promoting a cross-test contamination finding.

Unlinked watcher cleanup occurs only after two assertions; an early assertion failure may leave its infinite sleeper alive. Check suite lifecycle and demonstrate the failure path before promoting a leak finding; successful-path cleanup exists.
